'''''Anthericum liliago''''', the '''St Bernard's lily''', is a [[species]] of [[flowering plant]] in the [[Family (taxonomy)|family]] [[Asparagaceae]]. It is [[native plant|native]] to mainland Europe (not the British Isles) and Turkey, growing in dry pastures, stony places and open woods and flowering in early summer. In Sweden, the northernmost stable populations grows along the rocky shores of [[Sommen|Lake Sommen]] (58° N), albeit on occasions it has been found as far north as [[Uppland]] (60° N).<ref>{{cite web |title=Anthericum liliago Stor sandlilja |url=http://artfakta.artdatabanken.se/taxon/61 |website=Artdatabanken |publisher=[[Swedish University of Agricultural Sciences]] |accessdate=May 2, 2019|language=Swedish}}</ref><ref name=sommennat>{{cite web |title=Om naturum |url=http://sommen-naturum.se/om%20sommen.html |website=sommen-naturum.se |publisher=Naturum Sommen |accessdate=April 20, 2019|language=Swedish}}</ref>

==Etymology==
The specific epithet ''liliago'' means lily-like or lily-carrier. Like many plants whose common names include "lily", it is not closely related to the true [[Lilium|lilies]].

==Description==
It is a vigorous [[herbaceous]] flowering [[perennial plant|perennial]] with [[tuber]]ous roots, {{Convert|60|-|90|cm|ft|abbr=on}} high, with leaves narrowly linear, {{Convert|12|–|40|cm|in|abbr=on}} and producing [[racemes]] of 6-10 lily-like white flowers in Spring and Summer.
[[Image:Anthericum liliago June 2007-1.jpg|thumb|center|220px|St Bernard's lily]]

==Cultivation==
Best grown in well-drained soil in a sunny position, ''A. liliago'' can be [[plant propagation|propagated]] by seed or by division of the rootstock every 3 to 4 years. It is a slow starter but forms large clumps with time ([[USDA]] Zone 6). The cultivar 'Major' has gained the [[Royal Horticultural Society]]'s [[Award of Garden Merit]].<ref name = RHSPF>{{cite web | url= https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/216989/i-Anthericum-liliago-i-Major/Details
|title = RHS Plantfinder - ''Anthericum liliago'' 'Major' | publisher = Royal Horticultural Society | accessdate=12 January 2018}}</ref>
